question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which category of AIFs can be structured either as OPEN-ended or CLOSED-ended, while the others must mandatorily be close-ended?

answer.text: All three categories can be either open or close-ended

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.5: SEBI (AIF) Regulations permit Cat III AIFs to be either open-ended or close-ended. Cat I and Cat II AIFs must be close-ended with a minimum tenure of 3 years. The Trap: Option A reverses the rule. Option B is partial. Option D is false — Cat I/II cannot be open-ended. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II distributors) emphasises the mandatory close-ended feature; XIX-B covers the open-ended option for Cat III. XIX-C tests the contrast. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your investment strategy needs perpetual capital (e.g., listed equity long-short), Cat III open-ended is the only route. For illiquid private credit, stay close-ended — NAV-based redemptions would blow up the fund.
